newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai interbank rate rises again, baht up late.
newsitem.headline: Thai interbank rate rises again, baht up late.

text.p: The Thai overnight interbank rate was up further to 14.50-15.00 in late trade on Tuesday from 13.00-14.00 in early morning amid dollar buying and strong demand for funds from finance companies, dealers said.
"Finance companies were seeking to borrow a large amount of funds in the market today," said one dealer at a foreign bank.
Dealers said finance companies were heavily borrowing funds today in preparation for meeting the Bank of Thailand's reserve requirements due on Thursday.
All finance firms have to meet reserve requirements every Thursday.
Dealers said the lingering concerns about some finance companies' liquidity problems, first raised last month, had also caused banks to lend funds selectively to some of them.
The baht strenghtened to 25.515-25.522 to the dollar late from 25.530-25.540 in the morning on dollar's weakness abroad, dealers said.
"The dollar made a big swing against the Japanese yen today," said one currency dealer. "There was heavy selling of the dollar here after the U.S. unit fell below 114 yen."
One-month baht/dollar swap premium rose to 10.50/11.00 satangs per dollar late from 9.25/10.25 early amid tighter liquidity, dealers said.
The Bank of Thailand fixed the mid-rate at 25.53 to the dollar against 25.49 on Monday. The mid-rate of 25.53 is the lowest level since January 25, 1994 when the mid-rate was set at 25.54.
